events.text: The new House of Representatives first sits, which starts the five-year term.
events.note: Date from Wikipedia. Confirm it from the House Hansard or the Gazette.

events.text: Delma Thomas, NNP MP for St. Andrew North West, crosses to the NDC and joins the Cabinet.
events.note: Month from a secondary source. The crossing itself is confirmed by NOW Grenada (20 Jan 2025).

events.text: NNP convention: Emmalin Pierre becomes political leader, succeeding Keith Mitchell.
events.note: Wikipedia says she has led the party since December 2024, and NOW Grenada dates the convention to 15 December 2024. Confirm from party or Gazette records.

events.text: Peter David, MP for the Town of St. George, resigns from the NNP and sits as an independent. The NNP is down to 4 seats.
Peter David launches the Democratic People’s Movement (DPM).
The NNP has named 14 of its 15 candidates.
The DPM’s first congress names 8 candidates, with Arley Gill as deputy leader.
DPB Global projection: NNP 9 seats, NDC 6.
events.note: It says 9 seats but lists 10 constituencies. See the polls table.

events.text: A supplied NDC St. Patrick West post reports Carl Andall’s selection for St. Patrick East.
events.note: The supplied post has no public link and has not been independently checked; GBN subsequently reported the candidacy on 23 September.

events.text: GBN reports Nigel Degale as the NDC candidate for St. George North West and Carl Andall for St. Patrick East.
The Prime Minister says the NDC will present all 15 of its candidates on 4 October.
The DPM names Dishon Edwards for St. Patrick East and Rolanda McQueen for St. Andrew South East, bringing its slate to 10.
events.note: The linked report could not be independently checked; these two names remain provisional.

events.text: Governor-General Dame Cécile La Grenade dissolves Parliament on the Prime Minister’s advice, ending the fourth session of the Eleventh Parliament.
Nomination day: returning officers receive nominations from 9:00 a.m. to 12 noon.
The latest possible election date: the Constitution requires the general election within three months after a dissolution.

NNP.E: Named as the NNP candidate (also as “Teacher Lisa”) in a DPB Global commentary in The New Today, April 2026. Not yet confirmed by the party.

polls.note: An earlier poll, mentioned in the same letter. The fieldwork dates and sample size weren’t published.
Sourced through Wikipedia and Angus Reid; we haven’t found the original CADRES release.
Said the NNP led in 9 seats; it won 4. A later letter from the same pollster (3 Feb 2010) gives the national figures as 52–46, which doesn’t match this published 51–41.
Taken 14 months before the March 2018 election.

Only estimated voter numbers were published: NNP about 30,000, NDC 22,000–24,000, undecided 5,000–7,000. It says the NDC led by 12 points on 1 Dec 2025. Newspaper reports say the poll is under scrutiny.
